losers.name: aero_geometry
losers.rationale: The body's surface file, in the OpenFOAM install. It is part of the OpenFOAM tutorials (GPL-3.0-or-later, its origin before OpenFOAM not stated), so it is never copied into this Apache-2.0 repository: the gates copy it into their scratch only. A copy under the project was the rejected alternative.

lost.reason: the body's length in x, nose to the rear tyre; the wheelbase is the tutorial's and is what a reader of OpenFOAM's case compares with

losers.name: aero_ref_length_m
losers.rationale: m: the tutorial's own reference length (its forceCoeffs `lRef`, the wheelbase), used for the Reynolds number only: Re = 20 x 1.42 / 1.5e-5 = 1.9e6, past the 5e5 aero.regime asks for turbulent wall layers. The drag area needs no length. What lost is in PARAMS.

lost.reason: the tutorial's count; on 7 physical cores it needs --oversubscribe, and with other work on the machine each rank waits for a core

losers.name: aero_ranks
losers.rationale: MPI ranks for each parallel run. The machine the demo was measured on has 7 physical cores, and other work shares it: 6 leaves one. The pack's default is 8 (with --oversubscribe). The ranks move the time, and the mesh and the drag area a little (about 1e-6 of it, the pack's DEFAULT_RANKS note): the pack decomposes with `hierarchical`, so one mesh on one rank count gives one history.

lost.reason: Celik's example ratio; the finest mesh of the motorBike would hold about 22 million cells, past the pack's cap of 20 million
the effective ratio from the cells comes out under 1.3 (P0's box: 1.25 and 1.29), and the ladder fails before it solves

losers.name: aero_ladder_ratio
losers.rationale: The mesh ladder's ratio: each level's background block is 1.5 times finer in every direction, (32 16 12), (48 24 18), (72 36 27), and snappyHexMesh refines every cell with it. The tutorial's own ladder at 1.5 gave effective ratios 1.42 and 1.37 from its cells (2026-10-23), past the 1.3 Celik et al. 2008 ask. What lost is in PARAMS.

lost.reason: the pack's selftest baseline states it for its spheroid, whose band at the formal order is 15.7%; a drag area known to 20% does not answer R1's 0.35 m^2

losers.name: aero_gci_max_pct
losers.rationale: % of the finest mesh's drag area: the largest mesh error band (GCI) aero.mesh_independence accepts (the author's choice, design decision D3: common practice for RANS verification). This project's ladder ran on 2026-10-25 (500 iterations a level, 6 ranks): 0.29925, 0.29625 and 0.30206 m^2 on 358654, 926215 and 2674337 cells, and its finest mesh did not settle under 1% (U_I 1.98%). So the gate compared none of them and computed no GCI, and C7 reads Failing whatever this number is, for the level that did not settle. Their order (down, then up) is not resolved: the change between the two finest, 0.0058 m^2, is inside the finest's U_I, 0.0060 m^2. P0's ladder of the tutorial's own case (its box, block (20 8 8) and 1500 iterations a level, 2026-10-23) also had a finest level that did not settle (0.3075, 0.2964, 0.3007 m^2; U_I 1.09% on its finest).

lost.reason: measured on the base mesh only; the finest level's solve is estimated at about an hour on 6 ranks, so an hour would stop a healthy run and the ladder would read Skipped, not judged

losers.name: aero_timeout_s
losers.rationale: s each OpenFOAM tool may run before it is stopped with every rank, and the gate skips. The longest single run is the ladder's finest solve. P0's finest tutorial mesh (2.6 million cells) took 5613 s for 1500 iterations on 8 ranks, and this base mesh's 500 iterations took about 6 min on 6 ranks (2026-10-23): about an hour for the finest level's 500 on 6 ranks. This project's finest level (2674337 cells) took 1587 s for its 500 on 6 ranks (2026-10-25), and the whole ladder 3256 s. Three hours leaves room for a machine shared with other work, so only a hung rank reaches it. What lost is in PARAMS.

runs.t: The air around a motorcycle
This project finds the drag of a motorcycle with a rider. The body is the motorBike from the OpenFOAM tutorials. In the model, the air comes to the bike at
20 m/s
. On the road, the bike moves through still air at that speed.
What the person asked for
The bike and the rider must push through still air with a drag area of at most
(R1). The drag area is the drag force divided by the pressure of the moving air. It does not need a frontal area.
How the drag is found

OpenFOAM makes a mesh around the body and calculates the flow with the k-omega SST model. Guards check each step: the speed of the air, the box, the quality of the mesh, the solver history and the wall model. OpenFOAM also calculates the pressure on the surface and the paths of the air. ParaView draws them.
What the pictures show
The pictures show the flow on the base mesh, which has

cells. The colours on the body show the pressure coefficient Cp. The lines show the paths of the air, and their colours show the speed of the air. The wake pictures show the slow air behind the bike and the rider. The chart of the drag area shows how the value changed during the last part of the solver run.
What the check found
